behavioral_notes.observation: Manager (daemon Thread) boots the IoT Box: starts nginx, checks git branch, ensures SSL certificate validity, then POSTs {iot_box: {identifier, mac, ip, token, version}, devices: {...}} to /iot/setup on the configured Odoo server. The response contains a WebSocket channel string used to set up WebsocketClient. Manager then polls every 3 seconds; _get_changes_to_send() detects device list changes, IP address changes, and version changes, and re-POSTs whenever anything changes. Scheduled daily tasks run certificate renewal, log-level reset, and git-branch check.

Subscribes to an Odoo Bus channel, then dispatches incoming JSON messages by type: 'iot_action' routes to device.action(payload) on the matching iot_devices[device_identifier] Driver; 'server_clear' calls helpers.disconnect_from_server(); 'server_update' updates the remote_server conf; 'restart_odoo' calls helpers.odoo_restart(); 'webrtc_offer' forwards to webrtc_client.offer(); 'remote_debug' toggles ngrok tunnel; 'test_connection' calls helpers.check_network(); 'bundle_changed' calls upgrade.check_git_branch(). Action results are reported back via send_to_controller() POST to /iot/box/send_websocket.

Polls https://iot-proxy.odoo.com/odoo-enterprise/iot/connect-box with an exponentially-backed-off interval (starts 15s, max ~40s) to register the IoT Box and retrieve a pairing code. Once the user scans the pairing code in the Odoo backend, the proxy returns {url, token, db_uuid, enterprise_code}; _connect_to_server saves these to conf, calls manager._send_all_devices(), switches git branch, then restarts Odoo. Pairing code expiry is handled by setting pairing_code_expired=True.

Driver subclasses auto-register via __init_subclass__ into the global drivers list. Interface.run() polls get_devices() every _loop_delay seconds, calls update_iot_devices() which diffs added/removed identifiers against _detected_devices, then calls add_device() which iterates drivers sorted by priority, calls driver.supported(device), and starts the matching Driver thread. Unsupported devices are tracked in unsupported_devices dict and reported to Odoo if allow_unsupported is True.

PrinterDriverBase maps action names to methods via self._actions dict: 'print_receipt' decodes base64 receipt image, converts to 1-bit black-and-white via PIL, then calls format_escpos() or format_star() based on receipt_protocol. format_escpos() parses printer name to select raster (GS v 0) vs. column bit image (ESC *) mode, with optional scaling. 'cashbox' sends ESC/POS drawer-kick bytes. Job status is polled every second via _check_job_status(). Duplicate actions are suppressed via an LRU cache of action_unique_id values.

Daily scheduled task: reads the nginx-cert.crt, checks common_name != 'OdooTempIoTBoxCertificate' and expiry > now+10 days. If invalid, POSTs {db_uuid, enterprise_code} to https://www.odoo.com/odoo-enterprise/iot/x509 (with up to 5 retries) to retrieve a Let's Encrypt-style x509_pem + private_key_pem. Writes to /etc/ssl/certs/nginx-cert.crt and restarts nginx. Informs the Odoo database via POST to /iot/box/update_certificate_status.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (OWL/JS — IoT Box local web UI)
behavioral_notes.observation: 20 JS files, 0 XML templates, 16 OWL components rendered on the IoT Box local HTTPS homepage (iot_drivers.assets bundle). Components include Homepage, StatusPage, WifiDialog, ServerDialog, UpdateDialog, CredentialDialog, DeviceDialog, HandlerDialog, RemoteDebugDialog, SixDialog (SIX payment), TimeDialog. No Odoo backend OWL; this is a standalone SPA served from the IoT Box itself.

it_architecture.application: iot_drivers (IoT Box firmware runtime — hardware peripheral abstraction and Odoo connectivity layer)
software_services: Odoo Bus WebSocket subscription (channel from /iot/setup response)
data_objects: IoT Box conf file: server_url, token, db_uuid, enterprise_code, wifi_ssid, etc.
logical_data_erm: Interface -> Driver (1:N, matched by connection_type + supported())
information_flows: depends: (none — runs standalone on IoT Box, not as a standard Odoo addon)
Odoo server -> WebSocket -> IoT Box: iot_action, server_clear, server_update, restart_odoo, remote_debug, test_connection, bundle_changed, webrtc_offer
IoT Box -> Odoo: POST /iot/setup (registration), POST /iot/box/send_websocket (action results), POST /iot/box/update_certificate_status
IoT Box -> iot-proxy.odoo.com: pairing-code registration + polling
IoT Box -> www.odoo.com/odoo-enterprise/iot/x509: SSL certificate provisioning

capabilities: Hardware peripheral discovery and driver matching (USB, serial, network printers, scales, payment terminals, displays, keyboards)
Real-time bidirectional communication between Odoo and IoT Box via WebSocket
IoT Box provisioning: cloud pairing, SSL certificate management, Wi-Fi configuration
Receipt printing (ESC/POS and Star protocols, raster and column image modes)
Remote debug access via ngrok tunnel
Firmware self-update via git branch switching
Local IoT Box web UI (OWL SPA for status, devices, configuration)
value_streams: IoT Box boot-to-ready: power on -> connect Wi-Fi -> pair with Odoo -> download handlers -> start interfaces -> register devices
POS hardware action: Odoo sends iot_action via WebSocket -> Driver.action() dispatches -> device responds -> EventManager.device_changed() reports result back
information_concepts: IoT Box (identifier, MAC, IP, token, version)
Device (identifier, name, type, manufacturer, connection, subtype)
policies: Drivers auto-register via __init_subclass__; priority determines selection order when multiple drivers support a device
Actions are deduplicated via LRU cache on action_unique_id (256 entries)
toggleable decorator allows devtools conf to disable specific actions or longpolling for testing
require_db decorator prevents any outbound Odoo call if server URL or IP is not configured
Certificate renewed daily if it is a temp cert or expires within 10 days
stakeholders: Retail/POS operator (uses peripherals driven by IoT Box)
Odoo system administrator (configures IoT Box, manages drivers)
Odoo server (sends actions, receives device events)

classification.rationale: iot_drivers is a firmware/runtime infrastructure module that runs on a Raspberry Pi or Windows IoT Box. It has no business-process models (0 ORM models), no business logic, and no user-facing transactional flow. Its sole purpose is to bridge physical hardware peripherals to the Odoo server via WebSocket and HTTP, a pure IT infrastructure capability. APQC 8.0 Manage Information Technology is the correct category. The baseline 13.0 was incorrect.

standard_capabilities: Plugin driver framework (Driver + Interface base classes with auto-registration)
ESC/POS and Star receipt printing with raster and column image modes
WebSocket-based real-time action dispatch from Odoo to IoT hardware
Cloud pairing via iot-proxy.odoo.com (no local network configuration needed)
Automatic SSL certificate provisioning from www.odoo.com
typical_fits: Odoo POS hardware (receipt printers, cash drawers, payment terminals, barcode scanners, scales)
Standard pairing flow: scan QR code in Odoo backend -> IoT Box auto-connects
Firmware updates via git branch switching (nightly.odoo.com SHA1SUMS check)
common_gaps: Custom/proprietary hardware requires a new Driver + Interface subclass not included in this module
Windows IoT is a supported but secondary path (IS_WINDOWS guards scattered throughout)
WebRTC (webrtc_client) appears wired in but is a newer capability with unknown production coverage
drive_hints: curl http://<iot-box-ip>/hw_proxy/hello to confirm the box is reachable
curl http://<iot-box-ip>/hw_proxy/status_json to see connected proxy driver statuses
IoT Box local UI at https://<iot-box-ip> shows StatusPage / DeviceDialog components
